high_level_description: Wordless Lyonnais Jacquard silk illustration: two equal independent weaving stations share a neutral pulley relay carrying one sealed cloth parcel without entering either loom or touching its pattern cards, while each canut retains a separate workspace; precise woven geometry, silk red, blue and gold, no text, arrows or throne.

compositional_deconstruction.background: A high-ceilinged Croix-Rousse weaving hall forms one neutral shared space with tall uncurtained windows, pale plaster walls, exposed roof beams, and an open wooden floor. Two equal work areas occupy the left and right halves at identical scale, separated by a clear central gap used only for transport. All surfaces remain unlettered and unnumbered, with no signage, diagram panels, directional marks, flags, or hierarchy symbols.

elements.desc: Neutral overhead pulley relay made from one closed oval loop of cream cord and two identical brass wheels, suspended evenly between the work areas without a control booth. The mechanism contains no storage, loom, lock, pattern cards, seat, crown, or command lever; it can carry a parcel but cannot create or alter its woven design.

Single sealed silk parcel clipped to the lower side of the pulley cord, formed as a compact indigo roll with red end caps, gold binding thread, and one asymmetric woven rosette spanning the closure. The seal remains intact; the parcel has no writing, duplicate copy, open flap, control handle, or connection to either loom.

Left Jacquard handloom built from dark walnut with a vertical blue warp, gold shuttle, brass hooks, and one private stack of unmarked punched pattern cards secured beneath its frame. Its proportions and height match the right loom exactly; it remains mechanically independent from the overhead relay and produces its own geometric cloth.

Right Jacquard handloom built from dark walnut with a vertical red warp, cream shuttle, brass hooks, and its own unmarked punched pattern-card stack secured beneath the frame. It matches the left loom in size and status while producing a distinct striped cloth that never enters or controls the neutral pulley relay.

Left canut operating the blue-warp loom, light-brown skin, short black curls, cream rolled-sleeve shirt, indigo apron, ochre trousers, and dark shoes. Standing in profile with a focused expression, they hold the local shuttle while both hands remain within the left work area and away from the passing parcel and opposite pattern cards.

Right canut operating the red-warp loom, dark skin, close-cropped grey hair, indigo work jacket, ochre apron, cream trousers, and dark shoes. Standing in profile with an attentive expression, he inspects his own striped cloth while the sealed parcel travels between work areas without entering his loom or changing his local pattern.
